content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by the same mechanism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 3. Both trifluoperazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 4. Both trimipramine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 5. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate through mechanisms involving OATP1B3 and OATP1B inhibitors. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Trofinetide may increase plasma levels of substrates of these transporters. 6. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates should be avoided, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the efficacy of live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administer the live bacterial vaccine only after completing antibiotic therapy. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate and vandetanib both increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. If QT-prolonging drugs must be used together, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 10. Both vemurafenib and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Erythromycin may also increase vemurafenib levels. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Additionally, erythromycin lactobionate increases venetoclax levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor closely for venetoclax toxicities. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and verapamil increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Exercise caution when coadministering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 15. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Both vorinostat and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 17. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through mechanisms involving OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 21. Both albuterol and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Aluminum hydroxide increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the toxicity of amifampridine through mechanisms that may lower the seizure threshold. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of amikacin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Both apomorphine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 31. Both arformoterol and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 32. Both aripiprazole and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of atogepant through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The recommended dosage of atogepant with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce avanafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and associated adverse events. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours for patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Both azithromycin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Azithromycin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure.
